title: Optical Imaging of Isolated Murine Ventricular Myocytes
protocol: Add 68.96 g of NaCl, 3.57 g of KCl, 59.58 g of HEPES, 2.18 g of K2HPO4, 3.08 g of MgSO4 and 19.82 g of glucose to 800 mL of double distilled water in a 1,000 mL flask for Krebs-Henseleit buffer HEPES.
Bring the contents up to volume in a 1,000 mL volumetric flask after full dissolution.

Add 86.51 g of NaCl, 0.552 g of NaH2PO4, 2.03 g of MgCl2, 9.91 g of glucose, 4.03 g of KCl, 2.65 g of CaCl2, and 35.76 g of HEPES to 800 mL of double distilled water in a 1000 mL flask for Tyrode's solution.
Bring the contents up to volume in a 1000 mL volumetric flask after full dissolution.
Mix 100 mL of the 10x KHB-HB stock with 875 mL of double distilled water in a 1,000 mL flask.
Place the flask in a 37°C water bath.
Once the solution reaches 37°C, use NaOH to increase the pH to 7.39.
Bring the solution to volume in a 1,000 mL volumetric flask.
Sterile filter the solution using a vacuum filtration system.
Mix 100 mL of the 10x Tyrode's stock with 875 mL of double distilled water in a 1,000 mL flask.
Place the flask in a 37°C water bath.
Once the solution reaches 37°C, use NaOH to increase the pH to 7.39.
Bring the solution to volume in a 1,000 mL volumetric flask.
Sterile filter the solution using a vacuum filtration system.
Mix 100 mL of the 10x modified Tyrode's stock with 875 mL of double distilled water in a 1,000 mL flask and dissolve 3.07 g of L-glutathione reduced.
Place the flask in a 37°C water bath.
Once the solution reaches 37°C, use NaOH to increase the pH to 7.39.
Bring the solution to volume in a 1,000 mL volumetric flask.
Sterile filter the solution using a vacuum filtration system.
Add 855 µL of dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) to 25 mg of blebbistatin powder to prepare a 100 mM stock solution.
Aliquot out in 20 µL increments and store at -80°C for up to six months.
Make stopping buffer by adding 2 g of bovine serum albumin (BSA) and 1 vial of aliquoted blebbistatin stock to 100 mL of 1x KHB-HB.
Sterile filter the stopping buffer using a vacuum filtration system.
Make plating buffer by adding 5 mL of fetal bovine serum and 1 vial of the aliquoted blebbistatin stock to 95 mL of M199 HEPES.
Sterile filter the plating buffer using a vacuum filtration system.
Make myocyte culture buffer by adding one vial of the aliquoted blebbistatin stock and 4 ml of penicillin-streptomycin to 396 mL of M199 (25 mM HEPES).
Sterile filter the myocyte culture buffer using a vacuum filtration system.
Autoclave 2 pairs of Dumont tweezers, 2 pairs of Iris curved scissors, 2 hemostats, one pair of plastic surgery forceps, and six black braided silk 4-0 sutures.
Sterilize 22 x 22 mm² glass coverslips.
Place a single sterilized coverslip in each well of a six-well plate.
Expose the coverslips to UV light for 1 hour with the lid removed and the UV lamp on.
Thaw laminin stock solution on ice.
Add contents of one bottle to enough cold sterile phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) to reach a final concentration of 0.04 mg/mL.
Aliquot out 1.3 µL into autoclaved 1.5 mL centrifuge tubes.
Store the aliquots at -80 °C.
Thaw the working laminin solution on ice.
Aspirate 200 μL of laminin using a P1000 pipette.
Gently drag the pipette tip along one edge of the coverslip to facilitate attachment.
Expel the remaining laminin in the center of the coverslip.
Spread the laminin droplet across the coverslip in a circular motion.
Place the coated coverslip in a 37 °C incubator for at least 1 h and up to 24 h before isolation.
Turn on the circulating water bath.
Set the temperature so that perfusate has a temperature of 37 °C.
Rinse the Langendorff apparatus with 70% ethanol followed by two rinses with autoclaved double distilled water.
Fill reservoir with KHB-HB and oxygenate with 100% oxygen.
Prime the system by allowing oxygenated KHB-HB to flow into a 100 mL beaker.
Switch the 3-way stop-cock position once 50 mL of solution has flowed into the beaker to stop flow from the KHB-HB reservoir.
Pour 50 mL of oxygenated KHB-HB from the beaker into the collagenase reservoir.
Let the KHB-HB drain from the digestion reservoir until 5 mL remains in the collagenase reservoir.
Switch the 3-way stop cock repeatedly between reservoirs while priming to allow the lines to degas.
Use the degassing trap located on top of the heating coil after system priming to allow any remaining air to exit the system.
Make the collagenase solution by combining 100 mg of type II collagenase, 100 mL of oxygenated KHB-HB, and 2 vials of blebbistatin stock for rats.
For mice, combine 100 mg of type II collagenase, 40 mL of oxygenated KHB-HB, and 2 vials of blebbistatin stock.
Inject the animal with 1,000 U of heparin.
Wait 5 min after injection.
Anesthetize the animal with isoflurane using the open-drop method (1 cc of Isoflurane per 500 cc volume).
Euthanize the animal with a pentobarbital mixture (150 mg/kg intraperitoneal).
Rapidly excise the heart by making an incision below the xiphoid process.
Expose the thoracic cavity by cutting the diaphragm and pulling back the sternum using forceps.
Excise the heart above the ascending aorta and place it in cold KHB-HB.
Cannulate the heart using a stereo microscope and number 5 forceps.
Ensure the heart is submerged and the cannula was primed before excision to prevent emboli.
Position the cannula tip approximately 1 mm above aortic insertion into the ventricle.
Start the flow of KHB-HB by rotating the stopcock on the Langendorff apparatus.
Connect the cannula to the Langendorff system.
Perfuse the heart for 5 min.
Switch perfusion from the KHB-HB reservoir to the digestion buffer reservoir.
Set a timer for 5 minutes for mouse or 15 minutes for rat once digestion buffer reaches the heart.
Collect the perfusate in a sterile 100 mL beaker and refill the digestion buffer reservoir as needed until the digestion time has expired.
After digestion, separate the chambers of the heart with forceps and iris scissors in a sterile 100 mL beaker.
Place each chamber into a separate well of a six-well plate.
Pour 5 mL of collagenase solution into each well and immediately start mincing the heart tissue using scissors to produce approximately 1 mm³ chunks.
Gently triturate the minced heart tissue using sterile transfer pipettes until the solution turns cloudy.

Examine the cells under an inverted microscope. If the number of viable cells is greater than 80%, proceed to strain the cells into a 50 mL conical tube using a 100 µm cell strainer, ensuring a different tube and strainer for each heart chamber.
If the number of viable cells is less than 80%, check the time it took to cannulate. If the cannulation time exceeds 5 minutes, try another heart.
If not, assay new collagenase lots through the collagenase sampling program.
Pellet the cells by centrifuging at 215 x g for 2 min.
Resuspend the pellet in 10 mL of stopping buffer.
Centrifuge the cells again at 215 x g for 2 min.
Resuspend the cells in 5 mL of plating buffer.
Perform a cell count.
Adjust the milliliters of plating buffer to reach a final myocyte concentration of 2 x 10^4 cells per mL.
Remove laminin-coated coverslips from the incubator.
Aspirate the laminin droplet.
Plate 200 µL of myocyte suspension on each coverslip.
Place the plate in a 37 °C incubator (21% O2, 5% CO2) for 2 h to allow attachment.
After 2 h, aspirate unattached cells.
Add 2 mL of culture media to each well.
Culture the myocytes for up to 4 days.
Make a 2 mM fura-2 acetoxymethyl ester (fura-2 AM) stock solution by adding 25 µL of DMSO to 50 µg of fura-2 AM powder.
Aliquot out into 6 µL aliquots.
Take one aliquot of fura-2 AM and add it to 6 mL of plating medium.
Vortex the mixture thoroughly.
Remove a six-well plate of myocytes from the incubator.
Aspirate the media.
Add 1 mL of fura-2 media mixture to each well.
Cover the plate with foil.
Leave the plate at room temperature and wait for 15 min.
Aspirate fura-2 media mixture from each well.
Add 1 mL of Tyrode's solution to each well.
Cover the plate with foil.
Wait 20 min at room temperature for dye washout before imaging.
Make a 1.82 mM fluo-4 AM stock solution by adding 25 µL of DMSO to 50 µg of fluo-4 AM powder.
Aliquot the fluo-4 AM stock into 8.333 µL portions.
Take one aliquot of fluo-4 AM stock and add it to 6 mL of plating medium.
Vortex the mixture thoroughly.
Remove a six-well plate of myocytes from the incubator.
Aspirate the media from each well.
Add 1 mL of the fluo-4 AM media mixture to each well.
Cover the plate with foil.
Wait 15 min at room temperature.
Aspirate the fluo-4 AM media mixture from each well.
Add 1 mL of Tyrode's solution to each well.
Cover the plate with foil.
Wait 20 min at room temperature for dye washout before imaging.
Remove component A and component B from the membrane potential kit.
In a 15 mL conical tube, combine 50 µL of component B and 5 µL of component A.
Vortex to mix thoroughly.
Add 10 mL of plating media to the conical tube containing the voltage dye mixture.
Vortex again to ensure thorough mixing.
Remove one six-well plate of myocytes from the incubator.
Aspirate the media from each well.
Add 800 µL of the membrane potential dye mixture to each well.
Cover the plate with foil.
Wait 15 min at room temperature.
Aspirate the dye media mixture from each well.
Add 1 mL of modified-Tyrode's solution to each well.
Cover the plate with foil.
Turn on the microscope.
Turn on the arc lamp.
Activate the hyperswitch.
Enable the fluorescence interface system.
Connect the Myocam power supply.
Start the field stimulator.
Power up the computer.
Ensure excitation/emission filter sets are appropriate for imaging dye.
Prime the system by turning on the vacuum.
Fully open the hose clamp.
Gently plunge each 60 mL syringe being used in the manifold.
For calcium recordings, use Tyrode's solution.
For voltage recordings, use modified Tyrode's solution.
Turn heater on and set flow using roller clamp adjustment on perfusion tubing.
Make recordings at 36 ± 1 °C.
Open acquisition software.
Set parameters for correct imaging dye.
In the dark, remove foil from six well plate.
Place a coverslip in the pacing chamber with stimulator off.
Focus on myocytes using the 10x objective.
Start pacing by field stimulating at 1 Hz, 0.2 V.
Gradually increase voltage until 1:1 pacing is obtained.
Increase voltage to reach 1.5 times threshold.
Perfuse the cells for 15 min before recording.
Switch from the 10x objective to the 40x objective.
Focus on a cell that is following a 1:1 pacing.
Adjust the plastic shades so only one cell is in the field of view.
Place the area of interest box on well-defined sarcomeres using the software.
Start the acquisition software to initiate the excitation light.
Adjust the neutral density filters to obtain an adequate SNR.
